heading: 5. Core Profiles, Identifiers, And Conformance

heading: 5.1 Individual And Complete-System Conformance
text: 5.1 Individual And Complete-System Conformance

heading: 5.1 Individual And Complete-System Conformance
text: A deployment claiming conformance to this BCP as a complete Logos module system MUST establish its initial Module Loader provider through protected, non-recursive bootstrap.

heading: 5.1 Individual And Complete-System Conformance
text: After Runtime binds that provider, it MUST use it to realize the orchestration module under protected bootstrap policy.

heading: 5.1 Individual And Complete-System Conformance
text: Every subsequent local module implementation MUST also be realized through the bound Module Loader provider.

heading: 5.1 Individual And Complete-System Conformance
text: Runtime MUST NOT substitute an independently started implementation or pre-existing provider endpoint for Module Loader realization.

heading: 5.2 Profile Terminology
text: 5.2 Profile Terminology

heading: 5.2 Profile Terminology
text: Its owner MUST define the profile's scope, required algorithms or mechanisms, validation rules, failure behavior, and relationship to other profiles.

heading: 5.2 Profile Terminology
text: An implementation MUST NOT replace a specification-fixed profile with another mechanism.

heading: 5.2 Profile Terminology
text: It also MUST NOT override an explicit deployment or request selection merely because it supports another profile.

heading: 5.2 Profile Terminology
text: Terms such as product profile, host profile, security profile, isolation profile, audit profile, or platform profile MUST NOT create independent Core selection layers merely by being named.

heading: 5.3 Defined Profile Matrix
text: Production remote transport | `logos.remote.quic` | Optional to implement. | Deployment or Runtime policy may select it only when both endpoints support it. Selection MUST be explicit.

heading: 5.3 Defined Profile Matrix
text: Package realization | `lgx` | Optional individually; a conforming Package Manager MUST implement at least one package realization profile. | A request selects it with `source.kind` equal to `"lgx"`.

heading: 5.3 Defined Profile Matrix
text: Package realization | `nix` | Optional individually; a conforming Package Manager MUST implement at least one package realization profile. | A request selects it with `source.kind` equal to `"nix"`.

heading: 5.3 Defined Profile Matrix
text: A conforming Package Manager MUST implement at least one of the `lgx` or `nix` realization profiles.

heading: 5.3 Defined Profile Matrix
text: Failure of a selected profile MUST NOT cause fallback to another profile unless the owning specification explicitly defines that fallback as safe.

The specification MUST define: … whether support is mandatory, conditional, optional, development-only, or prohibited in production;

heading: 5.5 Rules For Additional Profiles
text: A normative specification SHOULD introduce another named profile only when a complete interoperable behavior cannot be expressed by an existing profile, ordinary typed field, or local deployment policy. The specification MUST define: … the complete data schema, algorithms, validation rules, and failure behavior;

heading: 5.5 Rules For Additional Profiles
text: A normative specification SHOULD introduce another named profile only when a complete interoperable behavior cannot be expressed by an existing profile, ordinary typed field, or local deployment policy. The specification MUST define: … how the profile composes with or excludes every related profile;

heading: 5.5 Rules For Additional Profiles
text: A normative specification SHOULD introduce another named profile only when a complete interoperable behavior cannot be expressed by an existing profile, ordinary typed field, or local deployment policy. The specification MUST define: … downgrade, fallback, and unknown-profile behavior;

heading: 5.5 Rules For Additional Profiles
text: A normative specification SHOULD introduce another named profile only when a complete interoperable behavior cannot be expressed by an existing profile, ordinary typed field, or local deployment policy. The specification MUST define: … the conformance tests or vectors needed for independent implementations.

heading: 5.5 Rules For Additional Profiles
text: A generic string, opaque byte string, configuration key, backend name, or policy label MUST NOT define a Core profile by itself.

heading: 5.5 Rules For Additional Profiles
text: They MUST NOT appear in addresses, discovery results, or negotiation fields defined by these specifications.

heading: 5.5 Rules For Additional Profiles
text: Unknown or unsupported profile identifiers MUST fail the dependent operation unless the owning specification explicitly permits the identifier to be ignored.

heading: 5.4 Deployment Profile Requirements
text: A complete deployment MUST document every applicable choice that the Core specifications assign to deployment. At minimum, that documentation MUST identify: … accepted representations of protected deployment inputs, their provisioning and validation rules, and when replacement or revocation takes effect;

heading: 5.4 Deployment Profile Requirements
text: A complete deployment MUST document every applicable choice that the Core specifications assign to deployment. At minimum, that documentation MUST identify: … the authority-policy input format, its administration, and the explicit permissions needed by deployed bootstrap and system-service integrations;

heading: 5.4 Deployment Profile Requirements
text: A complete deployment MUST document every applicable choice that the Core specifications assign to deployment. At minimum, that documentation MUST identify: … accepted-declaration selection and exact package/version pinning for package-backed module creation;

heading: 5.4 Deployment Profile Requirements
text: A complete deployment MUST document every applicable choice that the Core specifications assign to deployment. At minimum, that documentation MUST identify: … any protected attribute-source integration required by Capability Authority policy;

heading: 5.4 Deployment Profile Requirements
text: A complete deployment MUST document every applicable choice that the Core specifications assign to deployment. At minimum, that documentation MUST identify: … startup, application-attempt, drain and cleanup deadline policies, their start points, covered phases, logical failure effects and permitted escalation, including shared-process limitations;

heading: 5.4 Deployment Profile Requirements
text: A complete deployment MUST document every applicable choice that the Core specifications assign to deployment. At minimum, that documentation MUST identify: … configuration-preserving upgrade responsibility and verified-default acquisition;

heading: 5.4 Deployment Profile Requirements
text: The documentation MUST also identify Package Manager installation and inventory scope, shared-state coordination, and the protected administration of required operating-system integration material.

heading: 5.4 Deployment Profile Requirements
text: A required facility or enforcement constraint that cannot be supplied MUST fail the dependent realization; installation success does not prove that every placement can realize the package.

heading: 5.4 Deployment Profile Requirements
text: For user-facing approval that changes protected policy or grants, the deployment MUST document how its administrative path authenticates the approving principal and authorizes changes to protected inputs.

heading: 5.4 Deployment Profile Requirements
text: An approval presentation MUST distinguish authenticated operation and scope identifiers from caller-supplied or publisher-supplied descriptions.

heading: 5.4 Deployment Profile Requirements
text: Recorded requester provenance MUST remain distinct from the authenticated consumer whose authority authorizes an operation.

heading: 5.4 Deployment Profile Requirements
text: A deployment supporting external application activation MUST document its activation mechanism, admission policy, accepted application selection, presentation handoff, and failure behavior.

heading: 5.4 Deployment Profile Requirements
text: Activation MUST resolve to an accepted module declaration and preserve Runtime-owned identity, lifecycle, authority, and realization checks.

heading: 5.4 Deployment Profile Requirements
text: An untrusted activation source MUST NOT select an arbitrary implementation artifact, choose a module-instance identity, grant permissions, or bypass the selected realization constraints.

heading: 5.4 Deployment Profile Requirements
text: A complete-system deployment MUST realize the activated application through its bound Module Loader before application code invokes Logos contracts.

heading: 5.4 Deployment Profile Requirements
text: Arguments and presentation resources remain application input and MUST NOT establish consumer identity or Runtime authority.

heading: 5.4 Deployment Profile Requirements
text: A deployment-specific representation MUST NOT alter the meaning or validation requirements of values defined by the Core contracts.

heading: 5.4 Deployment Profile Requirements
text: Deployment documentation MUST state module-state protection at rest, access by other operating-system principals or same-identity processes, available secret-storage facilities, backup and synchronization exposure, restore and rollback behavior, and retention and deletion guarantees and limitations.

heading: 5.4 Deployment Profile Requirements
text: Instance retirement and package removal MUST NOT be described as state deletion unless a separate authorized operation performs that deletion.

heading: 5.4 Deployment Profile Requirements
text: Use of the non-production mechanisms identified in LOGOS-MODULE-SECURITY-CONSIDERATIONS Section 13 MUST be selected explicitly through protected deployment configuration.

heading: 5.4 Deployment Profile Requirements
text: A deployment enabling any such mechanism MUST identify itself as non-production in its deployment documentation and operator-facing diagnostics.

heading: 5.4 Deployment Profile Requirements
text: Build mode alone MUST NOT enable development trust or exemptions.

heading: 5.4 Deployment Profile Requirements
text: A non-production designation MUST NOT waive requirements of the claimed Core specifications or selected profiles.
